[inline-override dispatch] Spread pilot for #2388 — user-directed inline GPU round on a `proposed` task

VERBATIM USER ASK (this turn): "run inline now. and if it succeeds then move on to running the
entire issue. else wait"

Preceding turn, verbatim: "with qwen2.5 7b instruct do we get good spread on QA and math and code"

## Why this round exists

QA spread is MEASURED from banked #1739 rollouts (TriviaQA reliability 0.940, NQ-Open 0.934,
SimpleQA 0.035 mean / 91% zero-pile — dropped). Math and code spread for
Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct are UNMEASURED: only published aggregates under other protocols exist,
and the pooled code figure (0.504–0.535, recomputed by problem-count weighting over HumanEval
84.8 / MBPP 79.2 / BigCodeBench-full 46.1 Complete or 37.6 Instruct / LiveCodeBench 28.7) derives
its spread substantially from a mixture ACROSS benchmarks rather than demonstrated WITHIN-benchmark
dispersion — the #2388 risk-10 benchmark-identity confound. This pilot measures the real thing.

## Scope

200 items × K=5 rollouts × 3 surfaces (math, MCQ, code) at the production protocol: Qwen chat
template, temperature 1.0, zero-shot, sampled (not greedy). Per-benchmark reporting, never pooled
— separating within-benchmark dispersion from the mixture artifact is the whole point.

Output per benchmark: mean, SD(y), SD(true rate), reliability and ceiling rho via the
beta-binomial decomposition Var(p) = Var(y) - mean(y(1-y))/(K-1), plus the zero-pile / one-pile
fractions. Admissibility rule (pre-registered): a pool is admissible while NEITHER extreme
exceeds ~90% — the shape that disqualified SimpleQA.

## Compute-character pre-launch statement

- NO ACTIVATION CAPTURE in this round. The pilot measures the DV distribution only, so there is
  no store, no capture rig, and no large staging. This is the main cost reduction versus the
  Phase 1 shape described in the task body.
- Ops arithmetic: 3 surfaces x 200 items x 5 rollouts = 3,000 sequences. max_new_tokens 2048
  (math, code) / 1024 (MMLU-Pro, which rewards CoT per arXiv 2406.01574). Upper bound ~6.1M
  generated tokens.
- Batched helper: vLLM batched `LLM.generate()` — continuous batching, one call per surface.
  Never sequential HF `model.generate()`.
- Projected wall: ~15-30 min generation plus ~3 min model load on 1x H100. Estimated <= 1 GPU-h.
  This round IS the measurement, so no prior measured per-cell basis exists to cite; the estimate
  is bounded by the token count above and the pod is the smallest GPU intent (`eval`).
- Verification is CPU-side and programmatic on all three surfaces — no LLM judge, judge spend $0.
  math-verify for MATH answer equivalence; option-letter match for MMLU-Pro; unit-test execution
  for code (evalplus for HumanEval+/MBPP+; native harnesses for BigCodeBench / LiveCodeBench).
- Disk: no multi-GB staging. Datasets are small; model weights land in the pod HF cache.

## Lifecycle

Pod: to be provisioned as `pod-2388-spreadpilot` (intent `eval`, 1x H100), named in the
`epm:run-launched` note that follows once it exists. `keep-running` tag set BEFORE provision to

`proposed`, i.e. not an active status, so the auto-stop would otherwise fire through bootstrap).
Tag removed and the pod terminated via the gated `pod.py terminate` path once results are
harvested and verified.

Session-survival backstop: the 45-min `/issue-tick` cron is deliberately NOT armed — #2388 is at
`proposed`, which is not an ISSUE_ACTIVE status, and arming there would STALE-REDRIVE into a full
`/issue` re-spawn this round must not trigger. The backstop is instead the `[long-phase-heartbeat]`
cadence plus the keep-running tag and the re-attach handles recorded here and in the run-launched
note.

## Pre-run positive control (REQUIRED before any code number is believed)

The three code harnesses were validated on the VM against the datasets' own canonical solutions:
HumanEval 25/25, MBPP 25/25, BigCodeBench 25/25. BigCodeBench passed there because the VM has its
dependency set; the SAME control must be re-run ON THE POD before any code result is trusted, or a
missing import would read as "the model got it wrong" across every item and manufacture a false
zero-pile.

capture in this round, so there is no store to upload — outputs are small JSON committed to git.

[long-phase-heartbeat] pod=pod-2388-spreadpilot — MooseFS venv import wedge; local-disk venv rebuild in flight

## Status

Pod provisioned and RUNNING (1x H100). Bootstrap reached [10/11] and preflight FAILED on
`venv import-health: deep-import probe timed out after 180s` — the documented ambiguous
signature (`.claude/rules/gotchas.md` § MooseFS FUSE READ-wedge on the pod `.venv`).

## Discrimination performed (three probes, all bounded)

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `uv run python -c "import transformers"` (300s bound) | TIMEOUT, user CPU 11.8s |
| same, re-probed after cache warm (300s bound) | TIMEOUT, user CPU 10.2s — no improvement |
| `./.venv/bin/python -c "import transformers"` (150s bound, bypasses `uv run`) | TIMEOUT, user CPU 7.9s |
| spot probes: statfs, small-file read, `.venv/pyvenv.cfg` read, `.venv/lib` listing (8s bounds) | ALL rc=0, prompt |

Reads on `/workspace` ANSWER promptly, so the mount is not hard-wedged globally; the wedge is on
the venv import path specifically — the many-small-file tree. Cache warming did not help, which
rules out the "slow cold MooseFS venv read" branch the preflight error names as the alternative.
Bypassing `uv run` did not help, which rules out uv's per-invocation resolution storm
(the #1689 `UV_NO_SYNC` trigger).

## Disposition — NOT a pod swap

The runbook's remediation is terminate + fresh provision. Deliberately NOT taken as the first
move: a fresh pod re-rolls the same hazard on the same MooseFS mount, and the root cause is that
the venv lives on the network mount at all. Container disk (`/`, overlay) has 50 GB with 211 MB
used — ample.

In flight: a detached local-disk venv build on the pod (`/opt/build_venv.sh`, log
`/opt/build_venv.log`, launched via setsid), installing vllm + transformers + datasets +
math-verify + numpy + python-dotenv into `/opt/eps-venv`, with `UV_CACHE_DIR=/opt/uv-cache` and
`HF_HOME=/opt/hf` — every hot path off FUSE. Same principle as the #505 mitigation (route the hot
path off the mount). Model weights (~15 GB) also land on local disk; 50 GB holds venv + weights
with headroom.

If the local venv imports cleanly, the pilot runs against it and no pod swap is needed. If it
does not, the pod swap is the fallback and this note is the evidence trail.

## Cost note

1x H100 has been billing since ~17:20Z with no useful compute yet — the wedge consumed the
bootstrap window. No results at risk (nothing has run; nothing to upload).

## Unchanged

`keep-running` tag set; teardown still routes through the gated `pod.py terminate` path.
No activation capture in this round, so there is no store to lose.

## Steps

1. **Wait** for the launcher to exit — ONE blocking ssh, not a polling loop:
   `ssh ... 'while pgrep -f "[r]un_pilot.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 60; done'`
   (`-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=60`). If it is already gone, continue.

2. **Code-harness positive control — REQUIRED before believing ANY code number.** The three code
   verifiers were validated on the VM (25/25 canonical solutions each), but BigCodeBench passed
   there because the VM has its dependency set. Re-run the SAME control ON THE POD: for ~25 items
   per code benchmark, execute the dataset's own canonical solution through the harness and
   confirm it passes. A missing import on the pod would read as "the model got it wrong" across
   every item and manufacture a FALSE zero-pile. If canonical pass-rate is not ~100%, the code
   numbers are INVALID — report that and do NOT mark code admissible.

3. **Read the table:**
   `cd /workspace/explore-persona-space && PYTHONPATH=... /opt/eps-venv/bin/python scripts/issue2388_spread_pilot.py --report-only`

4. **Land the results.** Copy the JSONs to the VM repo at the same relative path, `git add` them by
   EXPLICIT path (never `git add -A`), commit, push. Verify the landing by reading the blob back
   from `origin/main`, not by the push line.

5. **Post `epm:progress`** on #2388 with the full table (all five benchmarks), the canonical-control
   result from step 2, the per-benchmark `frac_items_all_k_identical` and `unparsed_fraction`, and
   an explicit ADMISSIBLE/REJECT verdict per benchmark. Admissibility rule: neither zero-pile nor
   one-pile above ~90%.

6. **Tear the pod down.** `uv run python scripts/task.py remove-tag 2388 keep-running`, then
   `uv run python scripts/pod.py terminate --issue 2388 --name-suffix spreadpilot --yes`.
   This run wrote NO HF artifacts — its outputs are small JSON already committed to git in step 4 —
   so there is nothing for upload-verification to check; if the terminate guard refuses, pass
   `--skip-upload-verify` and record that reason in an `epm:progress` note (the sanctioned form for
   a run with no HF prefix). Do NOT pass `--approve`, do NOT set `EPS_ALLOW_COMPUTE_KILL=1` or
   `EPS_ALLOW_POD_TERMINATE=1`, and do NOT call the RunPod MCP delete tool. On any other refusal,
   surface the pod name + hourly burn and stop. **The pod must not be left idling.**

7. **Branch on the verdict** (the user's standing conditional: "if it succeeds then move on to
   running the entire issue. else wait"):
   - **PASS** — math500 and mmlu_pro are already admissible, so PASS means the code surface either
     clears the pile bar or is explicitly demoted to exploratory. Then spawn the full pipeline:
     `uv run python scripts/spawn_session.py spawn-issue --issue 2388 --auto`
   - **FAIL** — the code harness control fails, or every code benchmark rejects. Do NOT spawn. Post
     the finding and stop.
